The explore-more sheet works the same way it does in SwiftUI: attach it to an
article view controller pushed onto a
, and the SDK
replaces the back button with its own. On tap, the configured frequency
capping decides whether to present the sheet; dismissing the sheet — close
button, swipe down, or the error state’s Continue — completes the original
back navigation. The decision logic, frequency state, and sheet UI are shared
with the SwiftUI implementation, so the two behave identically.
Because Objective-C enums cannot carry associated values, the native
capping is expressed as
plus an interval:
Like the SwiftUI modifier, attaching is a no-op (with a logged warning) if
the SDK has not been configured, and replacing the back button disables the
interactive swipe-back gesture. For a modally presented controller, the
completed “back” is a modal dismissal instead of a pop.
Note that the attached controller’s
content
is irrelevant — the trigger is
the navigation-bar back affordance, so an article rendered in a full-screen
works exactly like a native one.
